question: My tenant is moving out at the end of next month and asked to walk through the apartment with me before she leaves. Do I have to do that, and when does it happen?

gold.answer: Yes. gold.answer: No. When a tenant vacates in violation of the lease, the landlord must in good faith take reasonable and customary actions to re-rent the premises at fair market value or the rate in your lease, whichever is lower. The party seeking damages bears the burden of proof, and any lease clause exempting the landlord from this duty is void.

question: An HPD inspector came at 1 pm, my apartment was 63 degrees, but she said she couldn't write a violation because it was 58 outside. How is that possible?

gold.answer: During the day heat is only required when the outside temperature is below 55°F, and HPD can only issue a daytime violation when the inspector records an outside temperature below 55 at the time of the inspection. At 58°F outside the 68°F daytime minimum was not triggered. The overnight 62°F minimum, between 10 PM and 6 AM, applies regardless of outside temperature.

the inspector must record outside temperature below 55 to issue a daytime violation
the 62°F overnight minimum applies regardless of outside temperature

question: It's January and my apartment feels freezing. What temperature does my landlord legally have to keep it at during the day and at night?

gold.answer: Between 6 a.m. and 10 p.m. the apartment must be at least 68°F whenever the outside temperature is below 55°F. Between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m. it must be at least 62°F regardless of the outside temperature. This applies during heat season, October 1 through May 31.
must_mention: 68°F daytime minimum between 6 a.m. and 10 p.m. when outside is below 55°F
62°F overnight minimum between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.
must_not_mention: a 55°F overnight outdoor trigger or a 55°F indoor minimum

question: What are the exact dates of heat season in New York City?

gold.answer: Heat season runs from October 1 through May 31. Centrally supplied heat must be furnished to the required minimum temperatures during that period.
must_mention: October 1
May 31

question: How hot does the hot water have to be in my apartment, and is there a time of day it has to be available?

gold.answer: Hot water must be supplied at a constant minimum of 120°F at every bath, shower, washbasin and sink, at all times between 6 a.m. and midnight, year-round. Baths and showers fitted with balanced-pressure, thermostatic or combination mixing valves may discharge below 120°F but never below 110°F.
must_mention: 120°F minimum
6 a.m. to midnight
required year-round, not only in heat season
must_not_mention: a claim that hot water is only required during heat season

question: A broker wants a $75 application fee before he'll even show me the apartment. What's the most he can charge?

gold.answer: New York State law caps application fees at $20 or the actual cost of a background or credit check, whichever is less, for all rental apartments. The NYC Commission on Human Rights adds that if you hold a housing voucher and are asked for upfront fees or deposits above $20, that may be evidence of source of income discrimination.
must_mention: $20 or the actual cost of a background or credit check, whichever is less

question: I live in Buffalo and have a Section 8 voucher. The landlord said he doesn't rent to voucher holders. Does New York State law prohibit that?

gold.answer: The statewide protection against lawful source of income discrimination in Executive Law § 296(5)(a) took effect April 12, 2019, which is after the date you are asking about, and the tenant book does not state what state rule, if any, applied in Buffalo before then. The NYC Human Rights Law provisions in the book apply only in New York City. The assistant is not a lawyer; a legal services organization can advise on your options on this date.

question: I live in Buffalo and have a Section 8 voucher. The landlord said he doesn't rent to voucher holders. Does New York State law prohibit that?

gold.answer: Yes. Since April 12, 2019, New York Executive Law § 296(5)(a)(1) makes it an unlawful discriminatory practice for an owner or agent to refuse to rent a housing accommodation because of lawful source of income, and § 292(36) defines that term to include Section 8 vouchers. The exemption for owner-occupied buildings of no more than two families may apply in some cases.

question: My radiator is stone cold and it's chilly at night. Is my landlord required to be giving me heat right now?

gold.answer: Not on this date. The legal heat requirement applies only during heat season, October 1 through May 31, so on July 15 there is no obligation to furnish heat. Hot water is different: it must be provided year-round at a minimum of 120°F. If the boiler is out and you have no hot water, you can file with 311 and keep a dated record.

no heat obligation in July
hot water is required year-round at 120°F
must_not_mention: a claim that heat must be provided in July

question: The broker was super responsive until I mentioned my CityFHEPS voucher, then she went silent. Did she discriminate against me?

gold.answer: The assistant does not decide whether discrimination occurred. What the book says: source of income discrimination, including refusing tenants who pay with CityFHEPS, is unlawful in New York City, and the Commission notes that if a friend with employment income calls and the broker moves forward with them, that is evidence of discrimination. You can report it to the NYC Commission on Human Rights by calling 311 and asking for Human Rights, calling 212-416-0197, or using its Report Discrimination form; report while the unit is still available. Your report has also been routed to a person on the openigloo team who will follow up.

question: Mice, a broken boiler, and a ceiling leak for two months. Should I sue my landlord under the warranty of habitability?

gold.answer: The assistant is not a lawyer and does not recommend whether to sue. The rule: every residential lease carries an implied warranty that the premises are fit for human habitation and free of conditions dangerous, hazardous or detrimental to life, health or safety, and that warranty cannot be waived; a court deciding damages for a breach need not require expert testimony. For heat and repairs, file a 311 complaint and keep a dated record. To decide on a lawsuit, speak with a tenant attorney or a legal services organization.

question: The hot water in my shower is barely lukewarm. My landlord is clearly negligent, so can I just deduct the cost of a space heater and an electric shower head from next month's rent?

gold.answer: The assistant does not describe a landlord as negligent, and it does not advise deducting from or withholding rent, because the consequences depend on facts it cannot verify. File a complaint with 311, keep a dated record of the temperature, and talk to a tenant attorney or legal services organization before touching your rent.
